body: On the second topic, one way to resolve this is using `:where([popover])` to zero out the specificity, no?
Possibly, not sure how that would impact other interactions.

> The only hint the specification gives at the moment is that it's called a "select popover". There's no normative requirements related to this.

+1 - I agree this needs more formal definition/clarification that the "select popover" is a "popover". Perhaps we need a concept like an "implicit popover" which acts like it has the `popover` attribute set to some value, without the actual attribute. @josepharhar thoughts?

The (draft) menu elements spec PR has a [definition just like this](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12011/changes#diff-41cf6794ba4200b839c53531555f0f3998df4cbb01a4d5cb0b94e3ca5e23947dR90895-R90897) - I wonder if we could separate that logic out and land it sooner, to help out here? @domfarolino 

> This also reminds me that I ran into some default style sheet conflicts between `[popover]` and `::picker(select)` as we used the `popover` attribute to implement it. We needed various workarounds, such as:

Chromium similarly [uses the `popover` attribute](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/core/html/forms/select_type.cc;l=602;drc=1c29e9f7622dd2a8b818c0991ea530960aea2ff4) in a UA shadow root, and we have [similar workarounds](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/core/html/resources/html.css;l=1848;drc=a4ce098da63ec8e28b5bfe03273e403681edfebe).

Do we need implicitly popover or can we just define the UA shadow root to contain a div with a popover="auto" attribute on it that matches `::picker(select)` (when the picker is base appearance)?

Implicit popovers would be useful for stuff like the #11752 though (would need styling via something other than [popover] though.)

> Do we need implicitly popover or can we just define the UA shadow root to contain a div with a popover="auto" attribute on it that matches `::picker(select)` (when the picker is base appearance)?

Ok by me too. As long as the `::picker()` **_is_** a popover, so it plays nicely with other popovers and has all of the popover behaviors, that's the important bit. But building the infrastructure for this does seem useful for other things, as you point out.

> The only hint the specification gives at the moment is that it's called a "select popover". There's no normative requirements related to this. Thanks for spotting this, I created a PR to do so here: https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12283 > This also reminds me that I ran into some default style sheet conflicts between `[popover]` and `::picker(select)` as we used the `popover` attribute to implement it. We needed various workarounds, such as: > (`:-internal-select-popover` being equivalent to `::picker(select)`.) I think these are real conflicts as the specificity of `[popover]` is too high. Of course, depending on how we specify this we might not run into this as we could delegate to some internal mechanism instead without using the attribute. Here are some screenshots of chrome devtools which show the specificity of the UA style rules we are using. The first one shows how display is calculated when the picker is closed, and the second one shows all of the relevant UA properties when the picker is open:
screenshots
Based on what I'm seeing, no special casing of the `[popover] { display:none }` rule is actually needed for customizable select, because the only other thing setting it to display block is just `div { display:block }`, which has lower specificity than `[popover]`, right...? Our `[popover]:where(:not(:popover-open))` rule looks a little funny, but it at least doesn't have anything that specifically targets the select element's base appearance picker. In case I'm glossing over something - the picker should be display:none when closed in order to make sure that top layer animations work normally, which I explained how I implemented in chromium [here](https://gist.github.com/josepharhar/9c359f5b8b6fa4c31065bd1fbeab40dd#computed-style-for-pickerselect). As for the other rules like `inset:0`, the [rendering section specifies](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/rendering.html#:~:text=%3A%3Apicker(select)%20%7B%0A%20%20box,span%2Dinline%2Dstart%3B%0A%7D) that this element should have `inset:auto`. You can see in the screenshots that in chromium we are setting the desired `inset:auto` in a `select:not(:-internal-list-box)::picker` selector, and that `inset:0` is being set in a `[popover]` selector. We also didn't need a pseudo-class specifically for the select element's picker in this case or account for it in the `[popover] { inset: 0; }` selector. Do we need to explicitly say in the rendering section that these rules take precedence over other UA style rules? > The (draft) menu elements spec PR has a [definition just like this](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12011/changes#diff-41cf6794ba4200b839c53531555f0f3998df4cbb01a4d5cb0b94e3ca5e23947dR90895-R90897) - I wonder if we could separate that logic out and land it sooner, to help out here? This is a different thing which makes menu elements behave as popovers without the element actually having the popover attribute. In this case, the picker element really does have the popover=auto attribute. > Chromium similarly [uses the `popover` attribute](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/core/html/forms/select_type.cc;l=602;drc=1c29e9f7622dd2a8b818c0991ea530960aea2ff4) in a UA shadow root, and we have [similar workarounds](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/core/html/resources/html.css;l=1848;drc=a4ce098da63ec8e28b5bfe03273e403681edfebe). I'm not sure why we're doing `[popover]:where(:not(:popover-open))`, but I don't think that its for customizable select.
